title: Optimization of hydroponic growth system and Na+-fluorescence measurements for tree species Pongamia pinnata (L.) pierre
author: Marriboina, Attipalli
materials: CoroNa-Green AM (Invitrogen) is a cell permeant Na+ specific fluorescent dye that exhibits a characteristic increase in green fluorescence upon binding to Na+ ions, with little shifts in its absorption/ emission maxima at ~492/516 nm wavelength. It has a wide application in cell physiology studies to visualize the Na+ homeostasis mechanisms in both plant and animal cells [8], [9]–10].

In the current study, Oh et al. [8] and Wu et al. [9] protocol was optimized to investigate Na+ ion localization in higher plants/ tree species (Fig. 2). Freshly harvested Pongamia roots were cut into 1 cm long placed in fixative solution (2.5% glutardehyde solution in 0.1 M MOPS buffer, pH 7.5) for overnight at 4 °C. Notably, Pongamia roots were hard to performing the sections. However, the fixative solution was helped to soften tissue. The segments were washed thoroughly with 50 mM MOPS buffer solution 2–3 times. Further, the segments were incubated in 5 µM Na+ specific probe CoroNa-Green AM (Invitrogen) and 0.02% pluronic acid in 50 mM MOPS (pH 7.0) for overnight at room temperature. The segments were washed thoroughly with 50 mM MOPS buffer solution 2–3 times before performing sections. The sections were immersed in propidium iodide solution (Invitrogen) (2 µM in 50 mM MOPS buffer) for 15 min before visualizing under confocal microscope. We were discouraged with our results when the sections were directly incubated with CoroNa-Green AM dye (Supplementary Fig. 2A). However, prior incubation of root segments with CoroNa-Green AM dye produced good results for Na+ imaging and quantification (Supplementary Fig. 2B).Fig. 2Comparison of the modified method and the old method of Na+ localization and Na+ fluorescence intensity measurements.Fig 2

steps.title: Prepare seeds from Pongamia pods
steps.instruction: Collect Pongamia pinnata pods (accession TOIL 12) from Tree Oil India, dry them in an incubator at 37 °C for 3 days, remove seeds with pruning secateurs, and select uniformly sized seeds.

steps.title: Sterilize and pre‑germinate seeds
steps.instruction: Sterilize the selected seeds in 1 % (v/v) sodium hypochlorite for 5 min, rinse thoroughly with sterile double‑distilled water for 3 h, place them on a sterile moist cotton bed inside an airtight container, and incubate in darkness for 10 days; radicle emergence indicates successful germination.

steps.title: Prepare Hoagland nutrient solution
steps.instruction: Make full‑strength Hoagland’s No. 2 basal salt mixture (Himedia), adjust the pH to 5.75 ± 0.02, autoclave at 121 °C, 16 lb inHg pressure for 30 min; note that full‑strength MS and 10 × Yoshida solutions gave poor growth and were not used.

steps.title: Initial hydroponic culture in 50 ml tubes
steps.instruction: Place each germinated seed just above the nutrient medium in a 50 ml Falcon tube (Genaxy), seal with parafilm, and grow for 10 days, ensuring the primary root reaches ≈10 cm and its tip does not touch the tube bottom.

steps.title: Transfer to 300 ml glass tubes
steps.instruction: Move seedlings to 300 ml vertical glass tubes (5 cm × 30 cm), grow for 15 days until the primary root reaches ≈25 cm; renew the nutrient solution daily.

steps.title: Transfer to 1000 ml glass tubes
steps.instruction: Before the root tip contacts the tube bottom, transfer seedlings to 1000 ml vertical glass tubes (5 cm × 60 cm) for another 15 days; each tube holds a single seedling, fitted with a rubber stopper and sterile non‑adsorbent cotton, covered with black paper, and the culture medium is renewed daily.

steps.title: Maintain growth environment
steps.instruction: Keep the culture room at 24 °C with a 16 h light / 8 h dark photoperiod and approximately 60 % relative humidity throughout the experiment.

steps.title: Apply salt stress to 30‑day plants
steps.instruction: For 30‑day‑old seedlings (n = 20 ± 30), increase NaCl concentration by 100 mM per day until reaching the target of 300 mM or 500 mM, thereby avoiding sudden osmotic shock.

steps.title: Fix root segments for Na+ imaging
steps.instruction: Harvest fresh roots, cut them into 1 cm pieces, and fix the segments in 2.5 % glutaraldehyde prepared in 0.1 M MOPS buffer (pH 7.5) overnight at 4 °C.

steps.title: Wash fixed segments
steps.instruction: Rinse the fixed root segments 2–3 times with 50 mM MOPS buffer.

steps.title: Stain with CoroNa‑Green AM
steps.instruction: Incubate the segments in 5 µM CoroNa‑Green AM (Invitrogen) plus 0.02 % pluronic acid dissolved in 50 mM MOPS (pH 7.0) overnight at room temperature.

steps.title: Wash after staining
steps.instruction: Rinse the stained segments 2–3 times with 50 mM MOPS buffer.

steps.title: Counterstain with propidium iodide
steps.instruction: Immerse the sections in 2 µM propidium iodide prepared in 50 mM MOPS buffer for 15 min before confocal microscopy.

steps.title: Acquire 2D confocal images
steps.instruction: Observe the stained sections on a Leica TCS SP2 confocal microscope, capture images on a 2D plane, and quantify cytosolic and vacuolar Na+ fluorescence with LCS software (average intensity ≈250 arbitrary units).

steps.title: Acquire 3D confocal stacks
steps.instruction: Perform Z‑stack imaging at 0.48 µm intervals, reconstruct 3D images, and measure Na+ fluorescence using LCS software.
